construct: Workers are generally healthy enough to enter and remain employed, whereas the general population includes persons unable to work because of illness or disability. Comparing an occupational cohort with the general population can therefore make workers appear to have artificially low morbidity or mortality, potentially attenuating harmful occupational associations.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: An employed cohort is selected for sufficient health to work, while the general population includes severely ill/nonworking persons; this produces the healthy worker effect.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: Immortal-time bias can create apparent benefit in observational cohorts, but no exposure classification requires outcome-free survival time in this design.
adversarial_second_pass.expert_reviewer_reversal: Lower mortality even for unrelated diseases plus exclusion of severely ill persons from employment specifically identifies healthy worker effect.
